subject.title: Require Codex scan artifact coverage proof

question: Should ClawHub treat model-reported exact file ranges as sufficient coverage evidence for an authoritative clean verdict, accepting that missing or malformed evidence makes benign scans fail closed and retry?
rationale: The code can enforce declared ranges, but automation cannot choose the marketplace trust standard or acceptable scan-availability cost; the branch also needs a human rebase across newer worker paths.

options.title: Accept after current-main rebase
options.body: Approve model-reported ranges as the present trust contract, rebase manually, and require fresh positive, incomplete, bundled-package, and retry-path runtime proof.

options.title: Require independent access telemetry
options.body: Pause this branch until the worker can derive coverage from observed file reads or equivalent non-model instrumentation before authorizing clean results.

options.title: Use advisory rollout first
options.body: Preserve current completion behavior while recording coverage failures diagnostically, then switch to fail-closed only after production compatibility data is reviewed.

recommendation.title: Accept after current-main rebase
recommendation.body: Approve model-reported ranges as the present trust contract, rebase manually, and require fresh positive, incomplete, bundled-package, and retry-path runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the coordinated implementation and runtime proof and are best positioned to rebase it once the trust policy is confirmed.
